## p100 — Enemy divisions approaching Belgrade

**Edition context:** p100 — Enemy divisions approaching Belgrade.

<a id="edition-cases-p100-p100--enemy-divisions-approaching-belgrade"></a>



**Status:** Earlier body verified after explicit erasure resolution and two-coordinate insertion. **Key:** `Nov1-3`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Armin, 2017-03-01, comment 13](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852373). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

<a id="edition-cases-p100-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited reconstruction:**

> Keine Stoerung durch Feind. Mittags 2 feindl. Div. im Marsch auf Belgrad.

**Meaning:** No interference by the enemy. At midday, two enemy divisions are marching toward Belgrade.

**Notes:** `feindl. Div.` means enemy divisions. Spaces and punctuation expand the telegram's `X` separators; the wording follows Armin's repaired reading. Its treatment of the invalid printed `T` and the two inserted coordinates remains conditional, as recorded below.

## p100 B — Bridges and wire lines through Budapest; report attributes interruption to Hungarian National Council

**Edition context:** Bridges and the wire connection through Budapest.

<a id="edition-cases-military-budapest-wire-break-bridges-and-the-wire-connection-through-budapest"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p100 B reports that bridges have been blown up and attributes an
interruption of the wire lines through Budapest to the Hungarian National
Council. It ends with the literal headquarters label `A.O.K.11`.
The edition establishes what this telegram reports; it does not independently
verify those events or identify the location meant by `DORT`.

<a id="edition-cases-military-budapest-wire-break-source-and-body"></a>

### Source and body

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p100, PDF p103](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [B crop](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_B.png)
is under a November 1 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) UKS v ZÖN (------ November 2nd)
RICHI-194
```

</details>

Manual transcription finds **194 valid coordinates**, matching the printed
length. An earlier 195-slot OCR extraction produced a garbled result; its
extra slot is not treated as a historical cipher error. The unchanged
published `Nov1-3` key fixes all 97 raw plaintext positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BRUECKENXDORTXGESPRENGTXDRAHTLEITUNGENXUEBERXBUDAPESTXDURCHSUNGXNATIONALRATXUNTERBJOCHENXAXOXKX11
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BRUECKENXDORTXGESPRENGTXDRAHTLEITUNGENXUEBERXBUDAPESTXDURCHXUNGXNATIONALRATXUNTERBROCHENXAXOXKX11
```

</details>

Readable German, expanding only the explicit abbreviation in brackets:

**Readable German:**

> Brücken dort gesprengt. Drahtleitungen über Budapest durch
> ung[arischen] Nationalrat unterbrochen. A.O.K. 11.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 118 | 24 / 4 | `V` → `X` | `DURCHSUNG` → `DURCHXUNG` |
| 130 | 27 / 1 | `V` → `D` | `UNTERBJOCHEN` → `UNTERBROCHEN` |

There are no source erasures, inserted coordinates or square changes. The
final **11** is unchanged in both the raw and repaired readings.

The adjacent [p100 C](#edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p100-c-direct-contact-while-the-wire-is-broken)
asks about direct communication and also says the wire is interrupted.
The separately printed B body is not merged with the earlier
[p100 challenge](#edition-cases-p100); that challenge's Belgrade reading retains
**Armin's 2017 comment 13** priority. A multipart relationship is not required
to verify this independent source frame.

<a id="edition-cases-military-budapest-wire-break-reproduce"></a>

### Reproduce

The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and

```sh

```

## p100 C — Ask when direct contact is possible; wire interrupted; raw BRSLAU/MEGLICH preserved

**Edition context:** Radio contact, operating times and an unavailable key.

**Related source pages:** [p137 D](137.md#source-p137-d), [p142 A](142.md#source-p142-a), [p150 A2](150.md#source-p150-a2).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-radio-contact-operating-times-and-an-unavailable-key"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four independent records describe a broken wire connection, timed
radio calls, an embassy receiving station and the local absence of an
`OSKACHI` key. They use unchanged previously published keys and complete
source frames. They are grouped by subject, not asserted to be one exchange.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [collected intercepts](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and
[certificates](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain exact source rows, headers, key provenance, image hashes, raw readings
and all local repairs. Printed page numbers are three less than PDF page numbers.

<a id="source-p100-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p100-c-direct-contact-while-the-wire-is-broken"></a>

### p100 C: direct contact while the wire is broken

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_C.png)
is under a November 1 heading, with this November 2 reception line:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) UKS v ZÖN (2.03 a.m., November 2nd)
2235 (1) AN LP
RIZI-158
```

</details>

All 158 coordinates give 79 fixed plaintext labels under `Nov1-3`, without
any repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WANNISTUNMITTELBARERVERKEHRMITEUCHXMUENCHENODERBRSLAUMEGLICHXDRAHTUNTERBROCHENX
```

</details>

The sender asks when direct communication with the recipient, Munich or
the place written `BRSLAU` will be possible, and says the wire connection
is interrupted. `BRSLAU` is naturally read as Breslau and `MEGLICH` as a
damaged spelling of *möglich*, but **both remain literal in the certificate**.
No missing plaintext letters are inserted. The separately printed
[p100 B](#edition-cases-military-budapest-wire-break) gives a longer wire-break report;
this does not by itself prove a single transmission or a specific route.

This is distinct from the [p100 challenge](#edition-cases-p100), whose earlier
Belgrade body remains credited to Armin.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-verify-and-prior-credit"></a>

### Verify and prior credit

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The independent standard-library verifier rebuilds every source witness,
checks raw domains and numerical fields, and prices substitutions separately
from source-dash fills. No source coordinate is inserted or removed and no
published square is changed. Re-encryption confirms this stated arithmetic,
not the unique history of a damaged word or the identities of station names.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit examples of these bodies; it does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority.

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p137_D.png)
has `RIZI-102`. Its upper sender initial is overprinted, so the header is
conservatively retained as:

<details>

```text
D) ?CO V OSM (1.55 November 5th,)
RIZI-102
NF NRO V OSM
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. Neither it nor the footer is used to resolve
the unclear upper callsign or the time's missing a.m./p.m. designation.
The two dots after the final cipher group `AX` are punctuation; the footer
is outside the 102-coordinate body.

All 51 raw plaintext positions are fixed under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
POTSAGENDA3SSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution, source **79: G→X**, changes the `3`
inside `DA3S` to `S`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
POTSAGENDASSSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> POT sagen, dass Schlüssel OSKACHI hier nicht mehr vorhanden.

It asks that POT be told the `OSKACHI` key is no longer available here.
The key name itself is unchanged. The message does **not** say why it is
unavailable, identify a specific square or rank order, give its operating
period, or connect it to a separate challenge ciphertext. Its presence
inside a telegram decoded with `Nov4-6` does not make `OSKACHI` another name
for that transport key.

The raw numeral `3` remains visible in the original reading and numerical
ledger. Its local word repair does not reassign the square's digit `3`.

### p142 A: 0430 calling signal, then listen again at 0645

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_A.png)
is headed November 6:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) NKJ ZÖN v LP (08.25 p.m., November 6th)
FUER ZÖN 1900 (6/11)
RIZI-128
```

</details>

All 128 coordinates and 64 plaintext labels are fixed under `Nov4-6`, with
no substitutions or fills:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GEBENSIEX0430X10XMINXVVVXDANNIHREFKSPRUNDHOERENSIEUNSWIEDERX0645
```

</details>

The instruction is to send **10 minutes of `VVV` at 0430**, then the

time zone is inferred from the evening reception time.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-radio-contacts-and-keys-p150-a2-receiving-station-in-the-embassy"></a>

### p150 A2: receiving station in the embassy

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p150_A2.png)
explicitly labels this **part 2**. Its first part has not been attached or
reconstructed in this edition:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (8.55 p.m., November 7th)
PERA OSMAINE 6/11
FUER EILKESE ZU SS D (5) 2200
2 TL RICHI-180
UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. The literal `OSMAINE` and `EILKESE` spellings
and the November 7 reception remain unchanged. The instruction separator
before `UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN` is outside the ciphertext.

The 180-slot source contains one dash and gives 89 fixed labels out of 90
under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPEGSSTMTXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADT?SSENCHIFFRITENXINMLLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

Six known-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPFGSSTATXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADRESSENCHIFFRIRENXINALLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

The receiving station (`EMPFGSSTAT`) in the embassy listens for the
recipient. The message supplies the literal name/separator field
`NAMEXQZXX`, asks for addresses to be enciphered, and says to call in every
period. **The precise name boundary within `QZXX` is left unresolved.**
`CHIFFRIREN` and `PERIDEN` remain literal spellings; no extra plaintext
letters are claimed. The opening `JEDOCH` is retained rather than inventing
the missing preceding clause.

Known-coordinate changes, all at zero-based source indices:
**23 X→V, 80 X→V, 86 F→A, 92 X→V, 150 A→V, 167 X→V**.
The separate printed-dash fill is **112 ?→A**. Two of those substitutions
jointly change one raw `E` to `F` in `EMPFGSSTAT`; the certificate does not
collapse their cost into a single coordinate repair.

</details>

## p100 D1 — Eleventh Army and German elements placed under Mackensen: first part

**Edition context:** Eleventh Army subordination to Mackensen.

**Related source pages:** [p101 A2](101.md#source-p101-a2), [p101 D2](101.md#source-p101-d2).

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-eleventh-army-subordination-to-mackensen"></a>



Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

A two-part telegram on Childs pp100–101 reports that the 11th Army and all
its German elements have been placed under `O.K. MACKENSEN` and asks for
orders. A second copy of the ending provides useful letter evidence but has
an extra five-coordinate group and a weak source glyph. The native reading
and the conditional copy analysis remain distinct.

<a id="source-p100-d1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-p100-d1"></a>

### p100 D1

The [D1 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p100_D1.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, received at an unspecified time on November 2, origin
`2312 (1) 2 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-136`. There are 136 slots, including the
printed `L` at source 39 and `C` at 56. The following page is explicitly
marked as a continuation.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENX11XARMEE?ITALLENDEUTSCHENTEILENISTLAUT?XHXLXRMX1A11127
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENX11XARMEEMITALLENDEUTSCHENTEILENISTLAUTOXHXLXRMX1A11127
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> O.K. Mackensen. 11. Armee mit allen deutschen Teilen ist laut O.H.L. RM 1A11127

This first part has 66/68 raw fixed positions. Filling `L39` as `D` and
`C56` as `A` gives 68/68 fixed positions with **no observed-coordinate
substitutions**. It ends in reference `RM 1A11127`, with the sentence
continuing in A2. The source does not supply additional words between the
reference and that continuation.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-evidence-and-attribution"></a>

### Evidence and attribution

The published `Nov1-3` square and ranks retain the credit of **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The current source and arithmetic
review is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier unreviewed OCR
candidates are retained in the [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/prior_evidence.json).
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed. The existing
[p100 challenge](#edition-cases-p100) is a separate A message and keeps Armin's earlier
body credit; its status is unchanged.

[Literal rows, key and source images](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/inputs.json),

that each readable passage preserves every non-`X` label in its cited stream.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-equal-cost-copy-readings"></a>

#### Equal-cost copy readings

After the declared alignment, the two endings have 128 identical observed
coordinates, two complementary masks, and two observed conflicts. At common
frame index 65, A2 has `V` and D2 has `F`; at 131, A2 has `X` and D2 has `F`.
There are four equally minimum common streams:

| Common word / reference | A2 substitutions | D2 substitutions | Combined substitutions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `BITTEP / 7011` | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| **`BITTET / 7011`** | **1** | **1** | **2** |
| `BITTEP / 70G1` | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| `BITTET / 70G1` | 2 | 0 | 2 |

Every row additionally uses the same two D2 source-mask fills and the
separately stated five exclusions. The chosen readable row combines the
`T` supported by D2 and the numeric reference supported by A2. Equal edit
cost alone does not select it, and the two physical copies do not prove
independent transmission histories.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-geometry-and-weak-glyph-limits"></a>

#### Geometry and weak-glyph limits

All **133 contiguous five-coordinate exclusions** in the 137-slot source
were evaluated against the selected common text. Starts **8, 9, 10, 11 and
12** tie at one observed substitution and give exactly the same raw and
edited streams. Their source-origin maps differ. Start 10 is the printed
group boundary used for presentation, not a unique historical loss or
insertion location. This finite test does not exhaust arbitrary five-coordinate
exclusions or alternative plaintexts.

The old OCR's **136-slot interpretation** is retained as an alternate
reading of the weak ink trace. Under that interpretation, the equivalent
132-slot copy model needs five observed exclusions, one newly supplied
coordinate, one source-mask fill and one substitution. It produces the same
final text. The text therefore cannot decide whether the weak fifth slot
was a printed character or a missing coordinate; the primary slot choice
comes from the image review.

</details>
